reachability.node_behaviour: either mode logs the error and returns from derivationBlock (derivation.go:315-316 local, :461-462 layer1) before WriteLatestDerivationL1Height (:521): the L1 cursor does not advance, every later poll fetches the same log and fails again, so derivation stops for good at the first such commit (no batch after it is derived or verified by this node)
public_schedule: L1, at the time of each commit: the submitter's commitBatch (selectors 0xd63b3549 and 0x4a8d544f of the then-current ABIs) was accepted by the deployed Rollup; I59's replay holds all 2954 commits

L1, pinned code: Rollup.commitBatch's _loadBatchHeader (contracts/contracts/l1/rollup/Rollup.sol:259) accepts each of the 2954 parent headers too (sol_loader's harness on the real parents: solidity_on_rejected); BatchHeaderCodecV0.loadAndValidate requires only length >= 249

node: derivationBlock (node/derivation/derivation.go:236) fetches the Rollup's CommitBatch logs in [start, end] (:263-286) and, per log: local verify mode (the default, config.go:43) calls fetchBatchInfoOutline (:310), whose BatchIndex on the parent (verify_local.go:67) fails on a 281-byte version-0 header (common/batch validate: length != 249); layer1 mode calls fetchRollupDataByTxHash (:456) -> UnPackData -> parseBatch -> ParseBatch, whose BatchIndex (batch_info.go:92) fails the same way
reachability.reachable_on_mainnet: only with a non-default start height. With no stored cursor and no --derivation.startHeight, the first run pins the start to the latest confirmed L1 block (derivation.go:165-176), and the --mainnet preset sets only the rollup address (config.go:142-143), so a default node never processes these historical commits. An operator who sets --derivation.startHeight (flags.go:172-176, DERIVATION_START_HEIGHT) at or below the L1 block of the commit of any of batches 2..7575, as a node deriving the chain from L1 since the rollup's deployment would, reaches it: local mode stops at the first of these commits in its range; layer1 mode stops at batch 1 already if its range holds it (error:other, below), else at the first of these.
reachability.upstream_report: for the human to decide (I21 report, Questions for the human)

target_findings.why: 2954 real mainnet commits (batches 2..7575) carry a parent header that the chain accepted and that the pinned Solidity loader accepts through the public commit function, while the pinned node's derivation rejects it at its first header step (node/derivation/batch_info.go:92:55, error:header_index); the frozen ok_sol and ok_go say the same of every one, so it realizes L_dom_hdr. A node whose derivation range holds these commits stops at the first of them (reachability)

go_errors: decompress batch bytes error:morph da zstd decode: invalid frame

reachability.node_behaviour: layer1 mode returns from derivationBlock (:461-462) without advancing the cursor, as above: derivation stops at the first such commit. Local mode's fetchBatchInfoOutline decodes no blob, so it does not stop there.
public_schedule: L1, at the time of each commit: the submitter's commitBatch (selector 0xd63b3549) with one blob, the all-zero blob (its sha256 is fa43239b...e471, the versioned hash 0x010657f3...4014 of Rollup.sol's ZERO_VERSIONED_HASH), was accepted; I59's replay holds the 8 commits (batches 1, 23, 25, 26, 27, 28, 271 and 310)

node, layer1 mode: fetchRollupDataByTxHash (:456) -> UnPackData (ok) -> ParseBatch: the header steps pass (the parents are 249-byte version-0 headers), RetrieveBlobBytes of the zero blob gives zero bytes and zstd.DecompressBatchBytes fails ('morph da zstd decode: invalid frame', batch_info.go:122-124)
reachability.reachable_on_mainnet: only with a non-default start height (as above) and --derivation.verify-mode layer1, with the range holding the commit of batch 1, 23, 25-28, 271 or 310.
reachability.related_hypothesis: HypZ (Dec(Enc x ++ 0^k) = x): the codec encodes the empty payload as nothing, and decoding zero bytes fails, so HypZ is false at x = the empty payload (A4, audit round M2/2); these 8 commits are its instances on mainnet
reachability.upstream_report: for the human to decide (I21 report, Questions for the human)

target_findings.why: 8 real mainnet commits, accepted by the chain, pass the header steps of the pinned node's ParseBatch and are rejected by a later step (error:other: decompress batch bytes error:morph da zstd decode: invalid frame); a node whose derivation range holds them stops at the first of them (reachability)

6 hostile headers pass the Solidity loader of every public entry point and fail the Go decoders (the real sides agree with ok_sol and ok_go); with the pinned code no public entry point commits such a header, so on hostile inputs alone this is a known limitation (the real commits of go_consumer show it on mainnet)
